Egypt has approved Karnak Textile for Ready-Made Garments LLC as a private free zone project, with $15 million investment in Sadat City.
The 31,535-square-metre factory is set to start commercial operations in May 2027 and create 3,500 jobs.
It will use at least 50 per cent locally sourced inputs and export all output to the European Union and US, supporting Egypt's apparel export base.

title: Netherlands manufacturing output rises 4.9% in May
summary:
Calendar-adjusted Dutch manufacturing output in May 2026 was 4.9 per cent above May 2025, matching April's annual rise. 
Seasonally and working-day adjusted output edged up 0.1 per cent from April, with growth seen in nearly 40 per cent of industrial sectors. 
Improved producer confidence gives sourcing teams another indicator to monitor supplier sentiment and near-term output expectations.

title: Polyester chips rise on feedstock tightness and restocking demand
summary:
PET bottle and fibre chip prices appear to have found a floor after weeks of declines, supported by stabilising PTA costs and firmer crude oil. 
Producers are reducing discounts as feedstock costs rise, signalling a gradual recovery. 
Buyers may be nearing the end of the recent low-price procurement window if upstream raw material strength continues.

title: US cotton export sales recover but remain below four-week average
summary:
US Upland cotton export sales rose 36 per cent to 66,400 running bales (RB) in the week ended July 2, led by Vietnam and India, while shipments increased 5 per cent to 230,100 RB.
New-crop sales also strengthened.
Pima cotton sales rebounded, but export shipments declined sharply from the previous week's seasonal peak despite stronger buying interest.

title: Drewry WCI rises to highest level since September 2024
summary:
Drewry's World Container Index rose 2.4 per cent to $4,639 per FEU in the week ended July 9, its highest level since September 2024, driven by stronger demand and firmer Asia-Europe freight rates.
Tight capacity, planned rate hikes, and limited blank sailings supported prices, while Middle East tensions continued to add uncertainty to global shipping.

title: Why is the EU’s €122 bn textile import bill twice its €61 bn exports?
summary:
Europe’s textile industry faces a structural trade imbalance, with apparel accounting for 84 per cent of the wider deficit despite strength in fabrics.
The EU’s new €3 parcel duty and tougher sustainability rules will test whether enforcement can match regulatory ambition. 
Without equal scrutiny of imports, Europe risks stronger regulation but a weaker manufacturing base.

title: China sets 17% carbon intensity cut in 2026-2030 plan
summary:
China issued a 2026-2030 carbon-peaking plan, targeting 17 per cent lower carbon intensity and 25 per cent non-fossil energy by 2030.
Factory measures cover cleaner energy, coal substitution, low-carbon industry, zero-carbon sites, circular economy and key-sector cuts.
Manufacturers and sourcing teams should track zero-carbon parks, factories, standards and carbon accounting changes.

title: ICE cotton weakens as profit booking, lower crude weigh on prices
summary:
ICE cotton futures fell for a second straight session as profit-taking and lower crude oil prices outweighed weather concerns and export demand.
The December 2026 contract settled at 80.63 cents/lb.
Traders stayed cautious ahead of the USDA's July WASDE report, while weaker US export sales and lower trading volumes added to market pressure.

title: Brazil's cotton export boom is redrawing Asian trade
summary:
Brazil shipped a record 217,000 tonnes in June (+63 per cent YoY); 96.3 per cent of Brazil-origin cotton flowed to Asian markets.
Turkey's imports rose 64.4 per cent year on year (YoY), while Bangladesh became June's top buyer (21.7 per cent), confirming a sourcing shift.
The buyer edge may narrow as Brazil's crop falls, global stocks drop to 71.1 million bales, and the US intensifies exports.

title: India QCI-NSIC pact to boost MSME market access
summary:
QCI and NSIC have signed a five-year MoU to improve quality adoption, competitiveness and market access for India's MSMEs. 
The pact links ZED Certification, MSME Global Mart, TEAM Initiative and SPRS into a unified support framework. 
ZED-certified firms will get digital commerce, ONDC onboarding, AI product cataloguing and export promotion support.

title: US T&A imports drop to $39 bn in Jan-May; Vietnam retains top spot
summary:
US textile and apparel imports fell 8.92 per cent to $39.13 billion in January-May 2026, according to the Office of Textiles and Apparel (OTEXA).
Vietnam remained the top supplier, while China's shipments declined sharply.
Apparel and non-apparel imports both weakened, reflecting shifting sourcing towards Southeast Asia amid tariff concerns and changing supply chain strategies.

title: US' Carter’s reports 86% sustainable cotton sourcing in 2025
summary:
Carter’s has released its annual Raise the Future Impact Report for 2025, informing about progress in its sustainability commitments. 
The report says over 86 per cent of 2025 cotton was BCI Cotton or organic, with over 60 per cent of sales tied to responsible cotton. 
It cut virgin plastic packaging 90 per cent from 2022, reached 90 per cent recycled content, and expanded takeback and recycling pilots.

title: US' Authentic names Experience Group as Lee's Europe partner
summary:
Authentic Brands Group has announced a long-term partnership with Experience Group for Lee across Europe, tied to its planned acquisition of the denim brand. 
Experience Group will operate Lee in Europe across menswear and womenswear sportswear, activewear and workwear. 
The agreement targets wholesale, retail and e-commerce growth after the acquisition closes in the second half of 2026.

title: US' Levi Strauss DTC momentum drives stronger Q2 results
summary:
Levi Strauss & Co has reported Q2 FY26 net revenue of $1.56 billion, up 8 per cent YoY, while net income rose 19 per cent to $95 million. 
DTC revenue increased 11 per cent and e-commerce sales grew 19 per cent. 
Backed by strong first-half performance, the company raised its FY26 revenue growth forecast to 7-7.5 per cent and adjusted EPS guidance to $1.46-$1.52.

title: Australian apparel imports fall while textiles gain in July-May
summary:
Australia’s textile and apparel trade showed mixed trends in July–May FY2025-26.
Apparel imports fell 4.74 per cent to Au$11.62 billion, while textile yarn, fabric and fibre imports increased.
Textile fibre exports rose 6.74 per cent, although May imports of apparel, textiles and fibres declined year on year, according to the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS).

title: EU’s July 19 compliance cliff rewrites global apparel sourcing
summary:
From July 19, brands selling into the EU can no longer destroy unsold apparel, while mandatory Digital Product Passports raise compliance across supply chains. 
With the EU accounting for 50.1 per cent of Bangladesh’s RMG exports ($19.7 billion), competitive advantage shifts from low-cost sourcing to demand forecasting, inventory precision and traceable data.

title: ILO workshop strengthens Jordan's migrant labour reforms
summary:
ILO and GFJTU held a three-day Amman workshop to strengthen migrant workers' representation in Jordan's trade unions.
Garment manufacturing was among sectors in focus, alongside construction, agriculture, services and domestic work.
Talks also covered fair recruitment, organising, grievance handling and access to justice for migrant workers.

title: Vietnam's textile & garment exports rise 0.9% to $18.8 bn in H1
summary:
Vietnam's textile and garment exports (excluding yarn and fibre) rose 0.9 per cent year-on-year to $18.86 billion in January-June 2026, while yarn exports increased 10.3 per cent to $2.29 billion.
Fabric imports grew 1.7 per cent to $7.67 billion, though cotton imports declined 3.1 per cent in value.
The country is targeting $50 billion in textile, garment, and yarn exports in 2026.

title: ‘FABRIC Cambodia II’ launched with German help amid tougher standards
summary:
Germany and Cambodia have launched phase II of a project to improve the latter’s garment, footwear and travel goods sector amid tougher global environmental and labour standards. 
FABRIC Cambodia II focuses on supply-chain transparency and compliance with global regulations, moving beyond factory-floor audits to embed sustainability through public-private policy dialogue and workforce training.

title: AAFA calls for no additional tariffs on footwear imported from Brazil
summary:
A top official of the American Apparel & Footwear Association recently testified at the USTR' Section 301 hearing on Brazil, urging against additional tariffs on footwear imported from there. 
Additional tariffs on Brazilian footwear would increase costs for American businesses and families without advancing the broader objectives of an American First trade policy,” he said.
